pathways.climate_pressure: Climate-related pressure on outer-island food and water security.
pathways.documented_impact: The UNDP assessment describes existing movement toward crowded Majuro and Ebeye.
pathways.fcv_mediator: Unequal land access and limited urban services can mediate settlement and resource pressures.
pathways.possible_consequence: Poorly managed movement could increase grievances and resource competition; violence is not established.
alternative_explanations: Employment, education, services and historical relocation also drive mobility.
pathways.uncertainty: Source-stated prospective mechanism in the 2023 assessment, not causal attribution or a forecast of violence.
resilience_factors: Migration can provide opportunities; inclusive service provision and customary conflict resolution are proposed buffers.
pathways.compact_statement: Outer-island livelihood stress may interact with uneven land access and crowded urban services; mobility can also improve opportunities.

gaps: Main directly checked consultation heat/GBV and tenure passages, UNDP conditional relocation/mobility mechanisms, and the historical World Bank ISR. No new observed climate-caused violence is inferred.

executive_assessment.text: Majuro consultations identify access barriers around Ajeltake–Laura, differentiated high-tide support gaps and participant-reported heat/GBV concerns; these are local accounts, not national prevalence.

Leasehold incentives and conditional relocation/resource pressures matter for adaptation design. Community solidarity and communication outputs add capacity, with seawall progress retained at its April 2025 vintage.
